newsitem.title: USA: Mass Turnpike might advance 2 debt sales to autumn.
newsitem.headline: Mass Turnpike might advance 2 debt sales to autumn.

text.p: The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority, which this autumn expects to refund $360 million of bonds, also might advance two big debt sales to that period, a spokesman for the Authority said on Friday.

Robert Bliss, the spokesman, explained that if market conditions were favorable, the Authority this autumn might sell all or part of $700 million of bonds for its share of the Central Artery project, although it does not have to raise the funds until December 31, 1998.

The Central Artery project, referred to as the "Big Dig," recently was projected to cost as much as $10.8 billion when finished. The Big Dig project, which involves replacing an elevated highway in Boston with a depressed roadway that will run approximately eight miles, will start carrying cars in 2002.

The spokesman explained that the Turnpike might not decide until autumn on when it will sell all of the new debt planned. "The $700 million contribution is not due until December 31, 1998, but if this a good time to go to the market, we could go with either a big piece of that or all of that," he said.

Similarly, the $260 million of tunnel notes are not due until 1999. "There is a need to pay off these (notes) with bond proceeds. Given the favorability of current interest rates, we have not made the decision but are wondering whether or not this will be a favorable time to advance pay," Bliss said.

The Massachusetts legislature this spring approved a bill splitting the Turnpike into two costs centers, a western cost center, a 123 mile section running from the New York border to Route 128, which bypasses Boston, and an eastern cost center, an over 12 mile-stretch that runs from Route 128 to the Central Artery.

As a result, the Turnpike Authority will refund about $360 million of bonds. About $260 million of debt was attributed to the Turnpike's new, western cost center, and around $100 million was assigned to the eastern cost center.
PaineWebber was chosen as book-running senior manager, and Goldman, Sachs as co-senior manager, for the refunding of the 1993 bonds.
To date that is the only sale that has been set for autumn.
